description: A guide to the Kumbh Mela: the legend behind it, the four sites at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik-Trimbakeshwar, how the cycle and the Ardh Kumbh work, the akharas and Amrit Snan days, the announced dates for Haridwar 2027, Nashik-Trimbakeshwar 2027 and Ujjain 2028, and how to plan a visit safely.
dek: The Kumbh Mela is among the largest religious gatherings on earth, held in turn at four river towns.

intro: According to Hindu tradition, drops of amrit (the nectar of immortality) fell at four places during the churning of the ocean: Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik. A Kumbh Mela is held at each of these in turn, at dates fixed by the positions of Jupiter, the Sun and the Moon, when bathing in the river is believed to be especially meritorious.

Millions of pilgrims, sadhus of the akharas (monastic orders) and visitors gather for weeks in temporary tent cities. UNESCO added the Kumbh Mela to its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.
quickAnswer: The Kumbh Mela is held in rotation at Prayagraj (Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati), Haridwar (Ganga), Ujjain (Shipra) and Nashik-Trimbakeshwar (Godavari). The last Maha Kumbh was at Prayagraj in January and February 2025. Announced next dates are the Haridwar Ardh Kumbh (14 January to 20 April 2027), the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha (main bathing in August and September 2027) and the Ujjain Simhastha (27 March to 27 May 2028).
takeaways: The four Kumbh sites are Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik-Trimbakeshwar.
Each site hosts a Kumbh about every 12 years; Prayagraj and Haridwar also host an Ardh (half) Kumbh.
The main bathing days, now called Amrit Snan, feature processions of the akharas.
Book stays early and plan for very large crowds.

sections.heading: How the cycle works
paras: Each site hosts a full Kumbh roughly every twelve years, following Jupiter's cycle. Prayagraj and Haridwar also hold an Ardh (half) Kumbh about six years after the full Kumbh. At Ujjain and Nashik the mela is called Simhastha because it falls when Jupiter is in Simha (Leo). Prayagraj also holds the Magh Mela every year in January and February.
The most important days are the Amrit Snan (formerly called Shahi Snan) days, when the akharas, led by the Naga sadhus, bathe in procession before the public.

sections.heading: Planning a visit
list: Decide whether you want the main bathing days (spiritually central but hugely crowded) or quieter days in between.
Book tent camps or hotels as soon as they open; official and private camps are set up for each mela.
Expect vehicle restrictions and long walks; wear comfortable shoes.
Carry ID; follow official apps and announcements for routes and bathing ghats.
Travel light and keep children and older relatives close.

sections.heading: Etiquette
list: Ask before photographing sadhus, and respect a refusal.
Bathe only at designated ghats and follow lifeguard instructions.
Dress modestly and avoid alcohol and meat in the mela area.
Do not leave litter in the river.

safety: Crowds at Kumbh bathing days are among the largest anywhere; follow police and volunteer instructions and use designated routes.
Agree a meeting point with your group in case you are separated.
Stay hydrated and carry basic medicines.
Use only official information for dates, routes and camp bookings.
packing: Light layers and warm clothes for winter melas
Water bottle, snacks and a quick-dry towel
A change of clothes for the holy dip
A small torch for early-morning bathing

faqs.q: Where is the Kumbh Mela held?
faqs.a: In rotation at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik-Trimbakeshwar.

faqs.q: When is the next Kumbh Mela?
faqs.a: The Haridwar Ardh Kumbh runs from 14 January to 20 April 2027, the Nashik-Trimbakeshwar Simhastha has its main bathing dates in August and September 2027, and the Ujjain Simhastha runs from 27 March to 27 May 2028.

faqs.q: How often is the Kumbh Mela held?
faqs.a: Each site holds a full Kumbh about every 12 years; Prayagraj and Haridwar also hold an Ardh Kumbh about every six years.
The main bathing days of a Kumbh, when the akharas bathe in procession; formerly called Shahi Snan.

faqs.q: Where can visitors stay during the Kumbh?
faqs.a: In official and private tent camps set up for each mela, or in hotels in the host city and nearby towns; book as early as possible.
An annual gathering at Prayagraj's Sangam in January and February, smaller than the Kumbh.

faqs.q: Is the Kumbh Mela a UNESCO heritage?
faqs.a: Yes. UNESCO inscribed it on the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.
